 Live Updates Updated Thu, Nov 12 2026 12:19 PM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Nvidia live updates: Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress following resignation
 Kif Leswing Annie Palmer Kevin Breuninger Samantha Subin Ashley Capoot This is CNBC's live coverage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation. 
 watch now VIDEO 1:25 01:25 Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving Squawk on the Street Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down as CEO of the chipmaker he co-founded 33 years ago and built into a $4 trillion company that powered the artificial intelligence boom, the company announced Thursday. 
 CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO.
 "The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," said board chair Harvey Jones in a release announcing the news.
 The company will begin the search for a permanent CEO to replace Huang and will consider both internal and external candidates, according to the release.
 Kress also provided a statement in the release, but Huang was not quoted.
 After a meteoric rise to fame due to Nvidia's central role in AI, Huang's dramatic fall has been even more rapid, following a series of stinging revelations about his romantic ties to a woman believed by the U.S. intelligence community to be a Chinese spy.
 Huang, 63, apologized on Sunday for being "unfaithful to my wife," though he provided no details about the affair with businesswoman Alice Huang, who has worked for a Chinese company and Nvidia customer called Megaspeed. Late Wednesday, The New York Times reported that the Nvidia CEO also had a separate affair, this one with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care at the chipmaker. Later that afternoon, The Times and other outlets reported that Nvidia's board met to discuss the company's future. 
 Huang's downfall also puts the spotlight on President Donald Trump , who formed a particularly close relationship with the CEO of what, until recently, was the world's most valuable company. Huang became a key voice on U.S. AI policy while pushing for issues that were in Nvidia's interest, such as preserving access to open-source AI, and lobbying to allow chip exports to China.
 Read more CNBC news on Nvidia

 8 Min Ago Schumer: Congress must demand answers from Huang and Nvidia
 U.S. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) arrives to the U.S. Capitol Building on Nov. 9, 2026 in Washington, DC. Finn Gomez | Getty Images Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., said Huang's departure does not obviate the need for him and Nvidia to answer to Congress.
 "Despite Jensen Huang's resignation, Congress must demand answers from Mr. Huang and others at Nvidia about how they may have put U.S. national security at risk," Schumer wrote in an X post.
 "The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset," Schumer wrote. 
 "Were government officials told not to investigate because of Trump's relationship with Mr. Huang? What did Trump know when he personally invited Mr. Huang aboard Air Force One? Americans deserve to know that those at the highest levels of power are putting America first, not their bottom line or their personal friendships," the Senate leader wrote.
 — Kevin Breuninger 
 9 Min Ago Democrats probing Trump's approval of Nvidia AI chip exports to China-linked companies
 US Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick listens as NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang speaks during the G20 Innovation Ministerial in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, on September 2, 2026. Matt Ramey | Afp | Getty Images Democratic leaders on the Senate Finance Committee and House Ways and Means Committee are launching an investigation into the Trump administration's approval for the export of Nvidia's advanced AI chips to Chinese government-linked companies.
 Their letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick announcing the probe was sent by Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore., and Rep. Richard Neal, D-Mass., the respective ranking members of the Senate and House committees.
 Wyden and Neal noted that, despite Trump's reported knowledge of U.S. intelligence showing Huang was in a relationship with a Chinese spy, his administration "did not appear to acknowledge this evident national security threat."
 "On the contrary: despite reportedly learning of Mr. Huang's compromising relationship last fall, President Trump granted Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 AI chips to China in December 2025 in exchange for a cut of the export sales," the letter read.
 They described a "scheme" in which Trump would let Nvidia sell Taiwanese H200 chips to Chinese companies, provided they undergo a security review in the U.S. and receive an export license, subjecting them to 25% U.S. tariffs. 
 "The Trump Administration's ostensible attempt to mask an unconstitutional export tax as a
national security tariff action — benefitting both Nvidia and the Chinese government — raises serious concerns within our Committees' jurisdiction over matters relating to taxation and tariffs," they wrote.
 — Kevin Breuninger 
 23 Min Ago Jensen and Lori Huang’s massive Nvidia fortune is jointly controlled. That just got complicated
 FILE PHOTO: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Lori Huang attend the 12th Breakthrough Prize ceremony gala in Santa Monica, California, US, April 18, 2026. Mario Anzuoni | Reuters Jensen Huang's $140 billion Nvidia stake is largely held by trusts that are co-owned with his wife, Lori, according to SEC filings.
 The arrangement further complicates Huang's sudden exit from the company, but could prove to be a stabilizing force for the shares, since the trusts make it more difficult for either Huang or his wife to quickly sell, lawyers told CNBC.
 Here is why ultra-rich founders use these trusts and how they could work in the event of a divorce.
 — Hayley Cuccinello 
 29 Min Ago A 'complicated' mood inside Nvidia as Huang departs
 The Nvidia headquarters in Santa Clara, California, US, on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Employees inside Nvidia are struggling to come to grips with long-tenured CEO Jensen Huang's departure, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC. 
 But the mood at the company is "more complicated" than the headlines depict, according to the person, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly.
 The person described employees in tears, noting that many had come to idolize Huang and regard him as integral to Nvidia's identity.
 The person also sensed a "more nervous energy" around leadership and expressed concerns that the noise around Huang's affairs could impact execution.
 The board, they said, is in a difficult position, figuring out how to protect Huang and the company, while also ensuring it doesn't drag down the business.
 — Samantha Subin, Spriha Srivastava 
 35 Min Ago Huang is 'Mr. AI'
 Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, speaking on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Sept. 28, 2026. CNBC Beyond its impact on Nvidia, Huang's departure has deep ramifications for the AI industry that has turned him into a global spokesperson and celebrity, traversing the globe in his trademark leather jacket, touting the power of advanced chips, models and agents.
 Huang has seeded the market with numerous companies that buy Nvidia GPUs, building his company's influence and establishing a deep roster of customers, beyond the hyperscalers. Nvidia has used its balance sheet to backstop leases and chip sales, and has become the centerpiece of the industry, acting as technology supplier, customer, investor, financier and partner to scores of AI companies.
 "He's Mr. AI. He speaks for the industry," said Jeff Christian, CEO of Christian and Timbers, an executive search firm. "He's connected financially to everybody either through partnerships, or through lending the money to buy chips."
 — Kif Leswing 
 40 Min Ago Nvidia's risky financial backstops in focus as CFO takes the helm
 The Nvidia logo is seen at the company's Taipei office in Taipei, Taiwan, November 12, 2026. Ann Wang | Reuters Nvidia's growing credit support mechanisms for its customers, often offered in the form of a backstop on a loan or other type of debt facility, have come under question in recent months as the chipmaker's exposure has ballooned. 
 According to its last quarterly financial filing in July, Nvidia had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet backstops for neoclouds, as well as $20 billion dedicated to leases it had signed with the intention of renting out data center capacity. That's all in addition to the whopping $105 backstop deal Nvidia offered OpenAI to rent SB Energy's planned Ohio mega data center campus in August .
 In recent months, Nvidia's standards for its partners to require a backstop have become more stringent. The Information reported that CFO Colette Kress was against the $105 billion OpenAI deal, for example.
 Adil Malik, a partner at Origin Partners, a digital infrastructure-focused M&A advisory firm, says he noticed a change in the standards Nvidia needed to support a backstop for his clients around three months ago.
 "The offtake language before, maybe a non-binding LOI [letter of intent] from an offtaker would be enough, and it didn't have to be a very well known one that's an established company or AAA rated," he said, stating that now, a letter of intent "is usually not good enough. There has to be some level of offtake commitment, whether it's a binding LOI or ideally an executed offtake contract. Binding LOIs have been even extremely difficult now."
 — Isabel O'Brien 
 46 Min Ago Nvidia's stock grew 14-fold in AI boom
 Nvidia's fortunes exploded after OpenAI released ChatGPT in late 2022, leading to soaring demand for the chipmaker's graphics processing units, or GPUs. Nvidia's stock is up about 14-fold since then, even with a recent pullback related to the Huang scandal and the broader sell-off in the AI trade.
 — Kif Leswing 
 47 Min Ago Hakeem Jeffries calls for classified briefing on Nvidia scandal, says Dems investigating
 US House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, Democrat from New York, speaks during a news conference at the US Capitol in Washington, DC, on November 12, 2026. Jim Watson | Afp | Getty Images House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said Democrats are investigating the Huang spy scandal as they prepare to take over majority control of the House and Senate.
 The incoming Democratic chairs of the House intelligence and foreign affairs committees "are leading the effort to get to the bottom of what has happened," said Jeffries, who is poised to be House speaker in the next Congress.
 "There certainly are more questions than answers," Jeffries said at a press conference on Capitol Hill.
 "We need a classified briefing made available to members of Congress as it relates to the Nvidia situation," Jeffries added. "And to the extent that our national security has been compromised, the American people deserve answers, and we're going to work to make sure that happens."
 Asked by CNBC for his reaction to Huang's resignation, Jeffries said it "was the right thing to do."
 "Now we have to get to the bottom of whether America's national security has been compromised," Jeffries said.
 — Kevin Breuninger and Irit Skulnik 
 51 Min Ago Analysts race to downgrade Nvidia
 Analysts are growing bearish on Nvidia after an espionage scandal led to the exit of the company's CEO and co-founder, Jensen Huang. 
 Several shops on the Street downgraded the artificial intelligence infrastructure stock, citing the leadership questions that are swirling around Nvidia in the wake of the scandal. 
 "We find it hard to advocate stepping in here in size as there will no doubt be more allegations to come (there is a trope that says if you find two ants in your kitchen the best estimate of the total number of ants in your kitchen is not two...), both from internal issues as well as headlines related to the business, new governmental investigations etc.," Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon said Thursday in a note to clients.
 Keybanc analyst John Vinh echoed that sentiment in his own note to clients. 
 "We believe Huang's departure represents a material increase in strategic, organizational, and execution risk that warrants a higher risk premium and lower valuation multiple for the stock," Vinh wrote. "While we expect core fundamentals to remain strong for the foreseeable future, we believe it will be challenging for NVDA to find a successor with the same leadership and strategic vision as Huang." 
 ‘A dark day for Nvidia’: Here’s what analysts have been saying about Jensen Huang’s departure — Liz Napolitano 
 52 Min Ago Huang and Nvidia's close relationship with D.C. expected to change
 U.S. President Donald Trump (R) greets Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, as Trump and AI executives hold a media briefing following a meeting on artificial intelligence outside the West Wing of the White House on September 29, 2026 in Washington, DC. Kevin Dietsch | Getty Images Huang had emerged as one of Trump's closest allies in the AI build-out. 
 In May, Huang joined Trump on a trip to China, and in August, while on stage at the All-In Summit to discuss AI safety and regulation, he took a call from Trump and put him on speakerphone.
 "I'm with you all the way," Trump told Huang and the audience.
 With Democrats poised to take over both houses of Congress and promising to investigate various matters related to Nvidia, Huang's status in Washington, D.C., was poised to change dramatically even before the affairs became public.
 — Kif Leswing 
 56 Min Ago Kress to gather Nvidia leadership today at company HQ
 Interim CEO Colette Kress will gather the company's executive team today at the chipmaker's headquarters in Santa Clara, California, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC.
 Kress will discuss leadership and continuity plans with the group of high-level executives, according to the person, who asked not to be named because the details are confidential. 
 — Seema Mody, Annie Palmer 
 1 Hour Ago Huang to testify before Congress ahead of Thanksgiving, Mast says
 Nvidia President and CEO Jensen Huang speaks to the media as he arrives for a meeting with the Senate Banking Committee on Capitol Hill on December 3, 2025 in Washington, DC. Anna Moneymaker | Getty Images House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast, R-Fla. told reporters on Thursday that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will testify before Congress ahead of Thanksgiving. 
 "He has agreed to come," Mast said. "We're in negotiations for which day."
 The hearing will likely be under oath and transcribed, with multiple committees involved.
 Mast said he told Huang that he would "subpoena him" if necessary. 
 Mast said Congress isn't ruling out "public hearings for other people or other things down road."
 — Samantha Subin 
 1 Hour Ago Retail traders buy the Nvidia dip
 Retail traders rushed in to buy Nvidia shares following Jensen Huang's resignation, with the stock drawing the biggest opening bid from individual traders ever recorded by Vanda Research. In the first 30 minutes of the regular session, retail traders bought a net $111 million of Nvidia shares, more than 40x a normal open.
 The buying on Thursday follows multiple days of strong retail demand for the chipmaker's stock. It was the most heavily bought security across Vanda's universe Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday this week, commanding multiple times more net buying than the next most-bought security. NVDA has accounted for 61% of all retail net buying this week. 
 Demand has also spilled over into leveraged products: Retail investors put $42.5 million into six 2x long Nvidia ETFs from Monday through Wednesday, one of the largest three-day inflows on record, Vanda said.
 — Nick Wells 
 1 Hour Ago Nvidia board hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate Huang's affair
 watch now VIDEO 4:18 04:18 Pres. Trump says he spoke to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang today Fast Money Jensen Huang denied allegations that he had compromised national security or Nvidia secrets after reports of the Alice Huang affair. 
 The news sparked concerns that Nvidia knew companies based in Singapore and Malaysia had been evading U.S. export controls in accessing its technology. 
 The board said on Tuesday that it had hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate the intelligence allegations.
 — Kif Leswing 
 1 Hour Ago Senate Leader Thune expects oversight after Huang resignation
 Senate Majority Leader John Thune, a Republican from South Dakota, speaks with reporters outside the Senate chamber at the US Capitol in Washington, DC, US, on Monday, Sept. 14, 2026. Pete Kiehart | Bloomberg | Getty Images Senate Majority Leader John Thune , R-S.D., said he expects Congress to conduct oversight of the Jensen Huang affair even after the embattled tech CEO's resignation. 
 "In this environment where there's some really high stakes when it comes to our national security, I would expect there would be some follow-up, yeah," Thune said when asked by reporters if there would be congressional investigations into the matter. 
 Thune earlier this week was reelected Senate Republican leader. The GOP will be in the minority come January, after Democrats won at least 55 seats in the upper chamber. 
 — Garrett Downs 
 1 Hour Ago Hugging Face CEO on Huang ouster: 'A really sad day' 
 Clement Delangue, co-founder and chief executive officer of Hugging Face Inc., during the Bloomberg Technology Summit in San Francisco, California, US, on Thursday, May 9, 2024. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue lamented Huang's ouster from Nvidia, writing in a LinkedIn post that it's "a really sad day." 
 Nvidia in September agreed to acquire Hugging Face, a leading platform for open-source AI models, in a deal worth about $12.9 billion . The company expects the deal to close in the first half of 2027.
 "This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened," Delangue wrote. "It's a really sad day!"
 He continued, "But I want to make one thing clear: we'll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let's go!"
 The Hugging Face deal, which is the second-largest in Nvidia's history, has attracted scrutiny from regulators. CNBC previously reported that the U.S. Department of Justice is probing the acquisition and how it could impact competition in the AI market.
 — Annie Palmer 
 1 Hour Ago Mast still has confidence in Lutnick, wants BIS investigated
 Howard Lutnick, US commerce secretary, during an executive order signing in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, DC, US, on Tuesday, March 31, 2026. Aaron Schwartz | Bloomberg | Getty Images House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast, R-Fla., told reporters on Thursday that he still has confidence in Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick despite reporting this week that he stalled President Donald Trump' s crackdowns on firms routing Nvidia chips to China .
 Mast also said he wanted Congress to investigate the role of the Bureau of Industry and Security, a subagency of the Commerce Department that manages and enforces export controls, in the Huang scandal. 
 The New York Times reported earlier this week that the company's general counsel, Tim Teter, claimed in emails to commerce investigators looking into Alice Huang's company that he'd been in touch with Jeffrey Kessler, who leads BIS. The commerce investigation into Huang's company, Megaspeed, was then transferred to the Justice Department.
 "The people that we deal with in BIS, those are the ones that are at the granular level of dealing with Nvidia and chips," Mast said.
 Mast said he hadn't spoken to Lutnick or Kessler since the revelations.
 — Justin Papp 
 1 Hour Ago Creative Strategies CEO Ben Bajarin: Huang was a 'trendsetter' for semiconductor industry
 watch now VIDEO 4:42 04:42 Huang was a 'trendsetter for the industry': Creative Strategies CEO Ben Bajarin Squawk on the Street Creative Strategies CEO Ben Bajarin called Huang a "trendsetter" and said his exit creates "a huge shakeup and an impact to the industry."
 "Anytime ... you lose a founder-level-type of charisma who really has been looked upon as the, this trendsetter for the industry, the spokesperson for this moment that we have in this technology build out, that's going to be a loss," Bajarin told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" Thursday.
 Uncertainty over who will ultimately take the helm at Nvidia only adds to the challenge, according to the Creative Strategies CEO. Bajarin sees VP of Nvidia's data center business Ian Buck as the most logical candidate to be Huang's permanent replacement, with an internal pick likely preferable to an external candidate. 
 "You have to have deep semiconductor expertise ... it's a very short list of people who can do that at this scale."
 "What they need to bring back is somebody who can normalize things and be that type of person who can keep the troops aligned, keep them convicted on what they're doing in their engineering, and preserve that culture," Bajarin said. 
 — Caleigh Keating 
 2 Hours Ago Nvidia stock is now pricing in a ‘leadership discount,’ says Landsberg
 Jensen Huang, chief executive officer of Nvidia Corp., speaks to members of the media following the company's "Japan AI Ecosystem" reception in Tokyo, Japan, on Thursday, July 16, 2026. Kiyoshi Ota | Bloomberg | Getty Images Nvidia could face sustained selling pressure as investors reassess the value of Jensen Huang's leadership, according to Michael Landsberg, chief investment officer at Landsberg Bennett Private Wealth Management.
 Landsberg described Huang's resignation as the worst-case scenario. While he called CFO Colette Kress highly capable and respected, he questioned how the innovation of Nvidia will evolve without Jensen.
 "Part of the value proposition of this stock was not just its chips, but Jensen's vision and ability to steer the company," Landsberg said. "The stock is now pricing in a leadership discount, as the Jensen premium evaporates," he said, adding that while it is possible for Nvidia to navigate this storm, it's likely going to take time.
 Landsberg said Nvidia can survive without Huang, but warned that "it may not be the star company and stock that it has been for the past three years."
 — Deena Zaidi 
 2 Hours Ago Janus Henderson's Buckley calls Huang resignation a 'clearing event' 
 watch now VIDEO 4:11 04:11 Huang resigning could be a 'clearing event' for Nvidia, says Janus Henderson's Jeremiah Buckley Squawk on the Street Jensen Huang's resignation could bode well for Nvidia shares, according to Jeremiah Buckley, equities portfolio manager at Janus Henderson. 
 "I think you could argue, given where the stock is, that this could be a clearing event for the company," he told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Thursday.
 Buckley said Nvidia sits in a strong financial position and keeping its strong talent pool remains "extremely important" in the next phase.
 "We think visibility is extremely high for 2027," he said. "That demand continues to be really strong. We think the product roadmap is solidified through 2028."
 — Samantha Subin 
 2 Hours Ago Nvidia set to invest $10 billion in Anthropic immediately following its IPO
 Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic, during an interview at Anthropic's headquarters in San Francisco, California, US, on Thursday, April 30, 2026. Jason Henry | Bloomberg | Getty Images Nvidia has become one of the most prolific investors in the AI ecosystem, and Huang's ouster raises questions about whether the company will continue to shell out capital to other AI startups.
 It faces its first major test next week, as the AI lab Anthropic readies for what is largely expected to be a blockbuster IPO . Nvidia has invested billions in Anthropic to date, and the chipmaker has agreed to purchase another $10 billion worth of its Class N common stock immediately following the offering, Anthropic said in an amended prospectus on Tuesday.
 The shares Nvidia would purchase are part of a private placement that will not be registered in the offering, the filing said.
 Anthropic will list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT." The company is planning to begin trading on Nov. 19, as CNBC previously reported.
 —Ashley Capoot 
 2 Hours Ago Shares of Nvidia-backed companies slide
 Intel , Marvell and other stocks in which Nvidia has invested in traded lower following Huang's ouster.
 Shares of Intel and Marvell both slumped more than 4%, while Synopsys stock fell 3%. Coherent stock also slid roughly 4%, and Lumentum stock fell 5%. Nebius shares dropped more than 19% after it reported earnings, and CoreWeave 's stock slid roughly 9%. 
 Under Huang's leadership, Nvidia has become a significant backer of technology companies across the AI ecosystem. 
 The chipmaker invested $5 billion in Intel last September and said it would team up to develop data center and PC chips with its beleaguered peer. Nvidia also invested roughly $2 billion each in Nebius , Marvell , Lumentum , Coherent and CoreWeave through a series of deals announced over the past year. 
 Nvidia has also announced equity investments in several of the frontier AI labs, including OpenAI , Anthropic , and SpaceX 's xAI . 
 — Annie Palmer 
 2 Hours Ago Trump says Tim Cook should replace Huang
 Apple CEO Tim Cook speaks with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang in the Great Hall of the People. Picture Alliance | Picture Alliance | Getty Images Trump weighed in on the ouster of his closest corporate ally — and suggested another one should take his place.
 "NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple," Trump wrote on Truth Social.
 "A Legend replaces a Legend!" Trump wrote.
 —Kevin Breuninger 
 2 Hours Ago AMD stands to benefit from Huang's exit
 Lisa Su, chair and chief executive officer of Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD), speaks during the company's Gamers Day event in Seoul, South Korea, on Wednesday, Oct. 7, 2026. SeongJoon Cho | Bloomberg | Getty Images Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia creates a new opportunity for top chip rival Advanced Micro Devices . AMD shares were up nearly 17% since Monday, when the markets opened to news of Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
 As a top competitor to Nvidia, AMD is the only other company that makes a full rack-scale system for AI. Its Helios racks compete directly with Nvidia Vera Rubin racks. 
 While Nvidia's systems have long led the industry, companies are seeking alternatives to the costly, supply-constrained Nvidia chips. AMD's Helios is now deployed at Anthropic, Meta , Microsoft , OpenAI and Oracle .
 "AMD is clearly the immediate beneficiary. But people need to realize AMD can't just instantly ramp up massive additional volume even if customers look to move its way," said Daniel Newman, CEO of the Futurum Group.
 Amid market jitters over Nvidia's leadership shakeup, more demand could trickle down to AMD. The question is whether AMD can supply everyone who comes.
 "If everyone turned tomorrow and went to AMD, AMD couldn't supply. We know this," Newman told CNBC in an interview.
 Lisa Su, the CEO of AMD, is Jensen Huang's first cousin once removed. Huang confirmed they are cousins at an event in 2024.
 WATCH: Exclusive first look at Helios, AMD’s first AI system to rival Nvidia Vera Rubin 
 — Katie Tarasov 
 2 Hours Ago House Foreign Affairs Chair Mast: Huang is open to testifying as soon as next week
 Representative Brian Mast, a Republican from Florida, speaks to members of the media while arriving for a House Republican Conference caucus meeting at the US Capitol in Washington, DC, US, on Wednesday, June 3, 2026. Eric Lee | Bloomberg | Getty Images Huang is willing to testify before Congress as soon as next week, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chair Brian Mast, R-Fla., told reporters on Thursday, soon after the Nvidia CEO resigned.
 Mast, Rep. Rick Crawford, R-Ark., who leads the House intelligence panel, and Rep. John Moolenaar , R-Mich., who chairs the House China Select Committee, had requested Huang's appearance before the three committees in a Nov. 4 letter. They gave Huang and Nvidia until the end of day Wednesday to respond.
 "We heard back from their team last night," Mast said. "We're negotiating which day it's going to be."
 Mast said the parameters of the briefing are still being worked out. It's not clear at this time whether Huang would testify publicly or in a closed-door setting. But Mast said the committees are urging his testimony soon.
 "We want to see him basically in a week," Mast said. "Sooner rather than later."
 Mast said that subpoenaing Huang is also not off the table.
 "If negotiations shut off and we don't think they're in good faith — okay, fine, do that. I'll just subpoena you for the next day," Mast said.
 — Justin Papp 
 2 Hours Ago White House says Trump maintains 'complete confidence' in Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick
 watch now VIDEO 3:05 03:05 Commerce Sec. Lutnick stalled Pres. Trump's Nvidia China chip curbs after talks, according to Axios Closing Bell: Overtime The White House defended Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Thursday following reports that he repeatedly blocked President Donald Trump's efforts to crack down on efforts to smuggle Nvidia chips into China.
 "Secretary Lutnick is a champion of President Trump's America First trade and tariff policies, which have secured almost 20 fair trade deals and trillions in manufacturing investments," a White House official told CNBC in a statement. "President Trump maintains complete confidence in the secretary and his ability to carry out the position as the most transformative Commerce Secretary in modern history."
 Lutnick has also clashed with Trump administration officials, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, over why the Commerce Department did not place Megaspeed on its trade restriction list, according to Axios .
 —Ashley Capoot and Megan Cassella 
 2 Hours Ago OpenAI raises $15 billion at $1.25 trillion valuation
 watch now VIDEO 3:56 03:56 Faber Report: OpenAI raised $15B at $.125 valuation Squawk on the Street OpenAI has raised $15 billion in its latest funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation, sources told CNBC's David Faber . 
 Nvidia has invested at least $30 billion in OpenAI. Ahead of its expected IPO in 2027 , OpenAI has continued to raise capital despite blockbuster revenue growth due to large amounts of spending. 
 Whether the frontier AI lab would attempt to continue to raise more capital was unclear. OpenAI was originally planning to raise up to $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation in the latest funding effort, before pulling back. The announcement also comes as its chief rival, Anthropic, prepares to go public next week. 
— Caleigh Keating 
 2 Hours Ago Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas thanks Huang for 'bold leadership'
 Aravind Srinivas, chief executive officer of Perplexity AI Inc., during the Bloomberg Tech conference in San Francisco, California, US, on Thursday, June 5, 2025. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas shared a post on X thanking Huang for 33 years of "bold leadership." Nvidia is an investor in the company.
 "You built a small startup into America's most valuable company, with relentless improvement," Srinivas wrote. "Your grit and perseverance should always be remembered. Your personal generosity with time and advice to founders like me has secured a bright future for America and AI."
 —Ashley Capoot 
 2 Hours Ago Binance's pardoned ex-CEO says Nvidia is making a mistake
 Changpeng Zhao, founder of Binance, attends the Viva Technology conference dedicated to innovation and startups at Porte de Versailles exhibition center in Paris on June 16, 2022. Benoit Tessier | Reuters Changpeng "CZ" Zhao, the co-founder of crypto exchange Binance, said Nvidia should not let Huang go.
 "It's a mistake for Nvidia to let Jensen resign," Zhao wrote on X.
 Zhao in 2023 resigned as CEO of Binance while pleading guilty to money-laundering-related charges. He was pardoned in October 2025 by Trump, who made roughly $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency-related ventures that year.
 — Kevin Breuninger 
 2 Hours Ago Analysts have been slashing price targets
 Since the dramatic revelations over the weekend, analysts have been slashing their price targets on Nvidia's stock in anticipation of major changes at the top ranks. At least 10 Wall Street analysts have turned more bearish this week, according to FactSet. 
 "With no successor publicly identified, we would focus on who leads and on what timeline, retention of senior leadership, and channel and export-compliance posture," analysts at Stifel wrote in a note on Wednesday. They lowered their target to $205 from $315, but kept their buy rating. 
 The stock is currently trading about $160. 
 Baird analysts on Wednesday cut their target price by more than half, from $500 to $200, and downgraded the stock to neutral, "until uncertainties regarding U.S. government action likely resulting from the upcoming congressional hearing are lifted."
 —Ari Levy

 Ranking member Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., speaks during a Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee confirmation hearing in Dirksen Senate Office Building on Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026. Evan Vucci | Reuters Huang's resignation is putting a spotlight on the web of financial relationships he built throughout the artificial intelligence agency.
